text: The 2022 loss of about 0.6 hectares (3.4% of the asset) of native forest on this 17.6-hectare rural property was detected by satellite imagery, but the specific cause cannot be determined from the available Earth-observation data. The change could have been due to harvesting, fire, storms, or other stand-replacing events, but the evidence does not confirm deforestation, land-use change, legality, or responsibility. The loss was mapped as part of an annual global forest monitoring dataset (Hansen GFC) and corroborated by a 2020 reference forest map (JRC GFC2020), but these sources only identify where tree cover was lost, not why. Additional ground-based or regulatory data would be needed to determine the cause.
